## Fig. 1. Study design and model system

![Fig. 1](../figures/main/fig1_design.png)

Fig. 1 | Study design and model system. **a**, The 52-atom cell of every Li6PS5Cl run (Li24P4S20Cl4, cubic, a = 10.2795 A; the lowest-Ewald-energy S/Cl ordering of the Materials Project cell), in an oblique orthographic projection, farther atoms lighter. The S/Cl arrangement is fully ordered, Cl on 4a and the free S on 4c; the AIMD reference simulates the same arrangement. The origin is shifted by 0.18 along each axis so that the 4 PS4 tetrahedra (P-S < 2.6 A, minimum image; 16 bonds) lie inside the drawn cell. The 416-atom cell is its 2x2x2 supercell. **b**, Study design (protocol amendment A3): every model is compared with DFT. Grey boxes, inputs and simulations; outlined boxes, the three comparisons, each marked with the figure that shows it. Against DFT labels (Fig. 2): 27 configurations (frames 100-900, 9 per source temperature) of the 52-atom, 50-ps MACE-MP-0 runs were labelled with Quantum ESPRESSO 7.1 (PBE) at the Gamma point (1 k-point) and on a 2x2x2 mesh (8 k-points); MACE-MP-0 small was fine-tuned once on each label set, and the forces and energies of MACE-MP-0 and of both fine-tuned models are compared with these labels on held-out configurations. Against AIMD (Fig. 3): MD with the two universal potentials (MACE-MP-0 small, the foundation model, and MatterSim; 52 atoms for 50, 100 and 150 ps and 416 atoms for 200 ps) and with the two fine-tuned models (the Gamma fine-tune at stage two, the 2x2x2 fine-tune at stage one; 416 atoms, 200 ps), all at 600, 800 and 1000 K, is compared with AIMD of the same ordered cell through the Li diffusion coefficient D at 600, 800 and 1000 K, without extrapolation. The AIMD reference (Deng et al., Chem. Mater. 29, 281 (2017); Extended Data Fig. 8) has 52 atoms, a = 10.10 A (a 5 % smaller volume than here), a 2-fs time step and 100 ps at each of 600, 800, 1000 and 1200 K. Fine-tuned against foundation (Fig. 4): the fine-tuned MD runs follow the protocol of the 416-atom, 200-ps MACE-MP-0 runs and are compared with them through the reading fixed in advance (protocol/analysis_plan.md). The Cl-excess series Li6-xPS5-xCl1+x (x = 0-0.75; 392-416 atoms, 150 ps) runs with MACE-MP-0 (Extended Data Fig. 9). Markers: red, the universal potentials; blue, the fine-tuned models, filled for the stage-two model and open for the stage-one model; black square, AIMD. Black and grey bars, the 2x2x2 and Gamma label sets. **c**, The 42 MD runs (n = 42: 33 published, 9 new; 19 with a surviving run log), one per series and temperature, grouped into the universal potentials, the fine-tuned models and the Cl-excess series. Dark cells: the 33 runs published in July 2026, re-analysed here from the same trajectories (pymatgen class R1 for every run, kinisi class R2; Extended Data Fig. 2). White cells: the 9 runs analysed here for the first time (MACE-MP-0, 52 atoms, 100 ps; MatterSim, 52 atoms, 100 ps; fine-tuned on 2x2x2 labels, 416 atoms, 200 ps). 'log': the July run log survives (19 runs) and the thermostat statistics recomputed from the trajectory were checked against it; for the other 23 runs they come from the trajectory only. Markers: colour and fill by potential as in b; shape by run type (circle, 416-atom production run; triangle, 52-atom run; inverted triangle, Cl-excess series). Sources: data/structures/config0.cif, data/dft/configs.csv, data/dft/qe_runs.csv, data/references/aimd_deng2017/transport.csv, results/reproduction_runs.csv, results/thermostat.csv.

## Fig. 2. Forces against DFT

![Fig. 2](../figures/main/fig2_forces.png)

Fig. 2 | Forces against DFT. The test set H3 consists of the 3 configurations held out by both fine-tunes (T600_f400, T800_f200, T800_f500; the subsets are mapped in Extended Data Fig. 5a); the reference is the 2x2x2 k-point label set unless stated. **a**, Force components predicted by the three models that drove the MD runs (identified by force fingerprints, Extended Data Fig. 7a) against the 2x2x2 labels. H3 atoms are coloured by element (n = 468 force components per model); the T22 and H2 configurations are drawn in light grey behind them (T22 is training data of both fine-tunes, H2 of the 2x2x2 fine-tune). Dashed line, identity; solid line, least-squares fit through the origin on H3, whose slope measures force softening. RMSE and slope on H3: MACE-MP-0 216 meV/A and 0.81; Gamma, stage 2 59.3 meV/A and 0.99; 2x2x2, stage 1 70.3 meV/A and 0.99. **b**, Force RMSE on H3 (meV/A) of all five models: large markers against the 2x2x2 labels and grey bars against the Gamma-point labels, each over all n = 468 H3 force components; small dots, the n = 3 H3 configurations individually against the 2x2x2 labels (156 components each). MACE-MP-0 216 (2x2x2) and 220 (Gamma); Gamma, stage 2 59.3 (2x2x2) and 60.3 (Gamma); 2x2x2, stage 1 70.3 (2x2x2) and 73.2 (Gamma); Gamma, stage 1 72.8 (2x2x2) and 73.8 (Gamma); 2x2x2, stage 2 57.1 (2x2x2) and 60.3 (Gamma). The three models on the left drove the MD runs; the two on the right were not used for MD. Grey band, the H3 label floor (16.3 meV/A): the RMSE of the Gamma minus 2x2x2 force components over H3, the force error that separates the two label sets themselves. With 3 held-out configurations no confidence intervals are given. **c**, Force RMSE on H3 against the 2x2x2 labels per element for the three MD models (n = Li 216, P 36, S 180, Cl 36 force components per model), with the per-element H3 label floor (grey bars; RMSE of the Gamma minus 2x2x2 force components of that element over H3: Li 8.0, P 19.3, S 22.5, Cl 13.5 meV/A). P carries the largest error (MACE-MP-0 480; Gamma, stage 2 117; 2x2x2, stage 1 148 meV/A). Panels b and c share a logarithmic axis. **d**, Energy error per configuration (n = 27) against the 2x2x2 labels after removing each model's constant offset, the mean error over the 22 T22 configurations (all configurations have the composition Li24P4S20Cl4), ordered by source temperature and frame. H3 (dark band) and H2 (light band) configurations are in full colour, T22 faint. RMSE on H3: MACE-MP-0 8.15; Gamma, stage 2 1.71; 2x2x2, stage 1 1.44 meV/atom (All27: 9.37, 1.43, 2.03 in the same order). The foundation model's centred error drifts with source temperature (mean +7.7 at 600 K, -0.4 at 800 K, -8.7 at 1000 K meV/atom). Grey band, the centred energy label floor: the RMSE over all 27 configurations of the Gamma minus 2x2x2 energies, centred in the same way (offset over T22). 'Gamma' and '2x2x2' denote MACE-MP-0 small fine-tuned on the Gamma-point labels (22 training and 5 validation configurations) or on the 2x2x2 labels (24 and 3); stage 1 is the best epoch before stochastic weight averaging, stage 2 the model after it. Fine-tuned models are compared with DFT and with the foundation model only. Sources: data/dft/configs.csv, results/label_floor.csv, results/cross_evaluation.csv, results/cross_evaluation_configs.csv, data/models/predictions_forces.csv.gz.

## Fig. 3. Li diffusion against AIMD

![Fig. 3](../figures/main/fig3_diffusion.png)

Fig. 3 | Li diffusion against AIMD. The reference is AIMD of the same ordered Li6PS5Cl cell (Cl on 4a, S on 4c) by Deng et al., Chem. Mater. 29, 281 (2017), re-analysed with the estimators and settings of the MLIP runs (Extended Data Fig. 8). MLIP runs: 416 atoms, 200 ps per temperature, a = 10.28 A; AIMD: 52 atoms, 100 ps, a = 10.10 A. One trajectory per model and temperature. Every D is the kinisi estimate (seed 0, fitted from a lag of 30 % of each run onwards); error bars, +/- 1 posterior s.d. The Gamma-label fine-tune ran MD with its stage-2 model (filled markers) and the 2x2x2-label fine-tune with its stage-1 model (open markers). **a**, Li D against 1000/T of the production runs at 600, 800 and 1000 K (circles joined by lines; where markers would overlap, MatterSim and fine-tune points are offset horizontally by at most +/-0.013 in 1000/T, MACE-MP-0 and AIMD points sit at their true 1000/T) and of AIMD at 600-1200 K (black squares; 600 K, 7.1e-7 +/- 3.1e-7; 800 K, 4.3e-6 +/- 1.3e-6; 1000 K, 1.7e-5 +/- 3.0e-6; 1200 K, 4.2e-5 +/- 7.0e-6 cm2/s). At 600 K the AIMD Li MSD is almost flat in the fit window (log-log slope 0.071): that point measures caged motion, not long-range diffusion (dotted segment). **b**, kinisi D of each production run divided by the AIMD D at the same temperature (circles; error bars, the two relative standard deviations added in quadrature) and the pymatgen D ratio (short bars to the right of each circle). At 800 / 1000 K: MACE-MP-0 5.1 / 3.2, MatterSim 1.9 / 1.9, Gamma fine-tune 2.1 / 1.8, 2x2x2 fine-tune 2.6 / 1.9. Grey column, 600 K, where AIMD is caged. **c**, Li mean-squared displacement against lag time at 600 and 1000 K, averaged over all time origins; grey band, the MLIP fit window (lag >= 60 ps); black bar, the AIMD fit window (lag >= 30 ps). Log-log slopes in the fit window at 600 K: MACE-MP-0 0.826, MatterSim 0.403, Gamma fine-tune 0.354, 2x2x2 fine-tune 0.507, AIMD 0.0708; at 1000 K: MACE-MP-0 1.04, MatterSim 1.07, Gamma fine-tune 0.949, 2x2x2 fine-tune 0.995, AIMD 0.998 (1 for diffusive motion). **d**, Li force softening slope of the three MACE-family models that ran MD (least-squares slope through the origin of model against 2x2x2 DFT Li force components on the 3 configurations held out by both fine-tunes, H3; 216 components) against their kinisi D ratio to AIMD at 1000 K (logarithmic axis; error bars as in b). Slope and ratio: MACE-MP-0 0.855 and 3.21, Gamma fine-tune 0.992 and 1.76, 2x2x2 fine-tune 0.992 and 1.86. n = 3 models, no fit. The 52-atom runs and a second 416-atom MACE-MP-0 run are in Extended Data Fig. 4. Sources: data/md/transport.csv, data/md/msd.csv.gz, data/references/aimd_deng2017/transport.csv, data/references/aimd_deng2017/msd.csv.gz, results/aimd_comparison.csv, results/cross_evaluation.csv.

## Fig. 4. What fine-tuning changes

![Fig. 4](../figures/main/fig4_finetune.png)

Fig. 4 | What fine-tuning changes. MD values are re-analysis values of the 416-atom, 200-ps runs at 600, 800 and 1000 K of MACE-MP-0 small (the foundation) and of its two fine-tunes on 27 DFT configurations. 'Gamma' and '2x2x2' denote MACE-MP-0 small fine-tuned on the Gamma-point labels (22 training and 5 validation configurations) or on the 2x2x2 labels (24 and 3); stage 1 is the best epoch before stochastic weight averaging, stage 2 the model after it. The Gamma-label MD run used the stage-2 model and the 2x2x2-label run the stage-1 model (identified by force fingerprints, Ext. Data Fig. 7a); filled markers, foundation or stage 2; open markers, stage 1. Every comparison here is model against model or model against DFT; the comparison of the same runs with AIMD is in Fig. 3. **a**, sigma(300 K) (logarithmic axis; bars, 1-sigma interval from the fit covariance) and Ea (+/- 1 s.d.) of the weighted Arrhenius fits of ln(sigma T) against 1/T (pymatgen D, n = 3 temperatures, 600-1000 K): MACE-MP-0 5.54 [4.18, 7.33] mS/cm and Ea 0.266 +/- 0.012 eV; Gamma-label run 0.454 [0.309, 0.667] mS/cm and Ea 0.335 +/- 0.016 eV; 2x2x2-label run 0.260 [0.186, 0.365] mS/cm and Ea 0.360 +/- 0.014 eV. Right, the reading fixed in the analysis plan before the analysis was run (protocol/analysis_plan.md, part C): f = ln(sigma_2x2x2/sigma_Gamma)/ln(sigma_MP0/sigma_Gamma) is the fraction of the fine-tuning slowdown recovered with the 2x2x2 labels (MP0, the foundation run); f < 0.25 reads 'not explained', f > 0.75 'explains most', otherwise 'partial', and the two fine-tunes are 'indistinguishable' if |ln(sigma_2x2x2/sigma_Gamma)| is below its 1-sigma uncertainty (the half-widths of the two log intervals in quadrature). f = -0.222 and ln(sigma_2x2x2/sigma_Gamma) = -0.555 +/- 0.513: sigma_2x2x2 lies below sigma_Gamma, on the side away from the foundation. |ln(sigma_2x2x2/sigma_Gamma)| exceeds its 1-sigma uncertainty, so the two fine-tunes are not indistinguishable. The reading is 'not explained'. Grey zones in the 2x2x2 row: where sigma_2x2x2 would have had to lie for 'partial' (0.848-2.96 mS/cm) or 'explains most' (above 2.96 mS/cm). The two MD runs used models of different training stages, so this reading is confounded with the training stage (c). **b**, kinisi D of each fine-tuned run divided by that of the foundation run at the same temperature (circles; error, the two kinisi relative standard deviations in quadrature; one run per model and temperature) and the pymatgen D ratio (bars). At 600, 800 and 1000 K: Gamma-label run 0.161 +/- 0.039, 0.407 +/- 0.047, 0.547 +/- 0.051; 2x2x2-label run 0.160 +/- 0.029, 0.511 +/- 0.062, 0.581 +/- 0.053 (pymatgen: Gamma-label run 0.324, 0.435, 0.543; 2x2x2-label run 0.281, 0.508, 0.579). Fine-tuning lowers the kinisi D to 0.16-0.58 of the foundation's; the two fine-tuned runs differ by at most 1.3 combined standard deviations at any temperature. **c**, Force RMSE on the 3 held-out H3 configurations (468 force components, all atoms) against the 2x2x2 labels for the four fine-tuned models, by training stage; colour, label set. Gamma 72.8 (stage 1) and 59.3 (stage 2); 2x2x2 70.3 (stage 1) and 57.1 (stage 2) meV/A. Ringed and joined by the dashed line, the two models that drove MD. Within a stage the label set changes the error by 2.5 (stage 1) and 2.2 (stage 2) meV/A (brackets); from stage 1 to stage 2 it changes by -13.5 (Gamma) and -13.2 (2x2x2) meV/A (numbers on the lines). The MD comparison of a and b therefore crosses a label-set difference of about 2 meV/A with a stage difference of about 13 meV/A. No error bars: with 3 configurations no confidence intervals are given (Fig. 2b shows the single configurations). **d**, Pressure offset of each fine-tuned MD model from the foundation. Horizontal, the DFT single points: model pressure minus MACE-MP-0 pressure on the same configuration, averaged over all 27 configurations (paired; shaded bands, mean +/- standard error of the paired differences, n = 27): Gamma, stage 2 -0.504 +/- 0.017 GPa; 2x2x2, stage 1 -0.461 +/- 0.016 GPa. The DFT pressure cancels in the difference; the mean pressure errors against the 2x2x2 labels are MACE-MP-0 +0.064; Gamma, stage 2 -0.440; 2x2x2, stage 1 -0.398 GPa. Vertical, MD: mean pressure of the fine-tuned run minus that of the foundation run at the same temperature (labels), with the standard errors of the two run means from 0.5-ps block averages (n = 400 blocks per run) added in quadrature (at most 0.005 GPa, mostly hidden by the markers): Gamma, stage 2 -0.371, -0.370, -0.347; 2x2x2, stage 1 -0.446, -0.423, -0.403 GPa at 600, 800 and 1000 K. The three temperatures of one model share their horizontal value and are offset by +/- 0.012 GPa for clarity. Dashed line, identity. Absolute mean MD pressures at 600, 800 and 1000 K (GPa): MACE-MP-0 -0.357, -0.023, +0.339; Gamma, stage 2 -0.728, -0.393, -0.008; 2x2x2, stage 1 -0.802, -0.446, -0.063. Both fine-tunes lower the pressure, in the single points and in MD, but the order of the two fine-tunes is reversed: the Gamma (stage 2) model lowers the single-point pressure more, the 2x2x2 (stage 1) model the MD pressure. No model was trained on stress, so pressures are diagnostic; the DFT configurations come from the 52-atom MACE-MP-0 MD at 600, 800 and 1000 K, in the cell of which the 416-atom cell is the 2x2x2 supercell, and every MD run keeps that cell fixed (pressure time series in Extended Data Fig. 1). Sources: results/transport_comparison.csv, results/transport_ratios.csv, results/cross_evaluation.csv, results/cross_evaluation_configs.csv, results/thermostat.csv, data/md/timeseries.csv.gz, data/dft/configs.csv.

## Extended Data Fig. 1. Temperature, energy and pressure of every MD run

![Extended Data Fig. 1](../figures/extended/ed01_stability.png)

Extended Data Fig. 1 | Temperature, energy and pressure of every MD run. All 42 runs (14 series, each at 600, 800 and 1000 K; Langevin thermostat, 1 fs step); the series are those of Fig. 1c. In a-c and e, colour is the target temperature, marker shape the run type (triangles, 52-atom cells; circles, the 416-atom, 200-ps production runs; inverted triangles, the 392-416-atom Cl-excess runs of 150 ps), and open markers are the runs of the 2x2x2-label fine-tune, whose MD used its stage-1 model (every other model is filled). In a-c, a black outline marks the runs whose July run log survives (19 of 42); the statistics of the other 23 come from the trajectory only. Instantaneous temperature from the kinetic energy with 3N degrees of freedom; pressure -tr(stress)/3 + N k_B T / V. 'Gamma' and '2x2x2' are the MACE-MP-0 fine-tunes on the two DFT label sets; x is the Cl excess of Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). **a**, Mean temperature minus the target, n = 42 runs. Error bars, standard error of the mean from 5-ps block averages (the standard deviation of the 10-40 block means of a run divided by the square root of their number). The 52-atom runs lie on average +12.2 K (+1.5 %) from the target (range -2.5 to +25.3 K; 6 of 18 more than two standard errors above it and 0 below), the 392-416-atom runs +0.8 K (+0.1 %; range -5.2 to +4.6 K; 2 of 24 beyond two standard errors). **b**, Relative temperature fluctuation std(T)/T of each run (n = 42; the standard deviation of the instantaneous temperature over the production run, no error bars) against the canonical value sqrt(2/(3N)) (black bars, for the atom count of each series; logarithmic axis). The ratio of the two is 0.95-1.15 over all runs. **c**, Drift of the potential energy per atom (n = 42), the slope of a straight-line fit against time over the production run. Error bars, standard error of that slope from 5-ps block averages; 4 of 42 drifts exceed two standard errors (largest 0.156 meV/atom/ps). **d**, Temperature, potential energy per atom (minus its run mean) and pressure of the four 416-atom, 200-ps production runs at 1000 K (n = 4; colour, the model that drove the run), as 0.5-ps block means (thin lines) and 5-ps block means (thick lines); temperature 910-1096 K; dashed lines, the target temperature and the run mean of the energy. Mean pressure: +0.34 (MACE-MP-0), +0.67 (MatterSim), -0.01 (Gamma, stage 2) and -0.06 (2x2x2, stage 1) GPa. **e**, Statistics recomputed from the trajectories minus the values in the July run logs, for the n = 19 runs whose log survives. Grey bands, the tolerance of protocol item 7: |d mean T| <= 1 K for 52 atoms and 0.2 K for 392-416 atoms (the logs include one extra sample at step 0 and round to 0.1 K); mean energy and drift within one unit of the logged rounding (10^-4 eV/atom and 10^-3 meV/atom/ps). The mean temperature agrees in 19 of 19 runs and the mean energy in 19 of 19. The drift agrees in 15 of 19; it does not in 4 52-atom, 50-ps runs (MACE-MP-0 800 K, MACE-MP-0 1000 K, MatterSim 800 K, MatterSim 1000 K; the markers below the band), which differ by 1.20-1.49 x 10^-3 meV/atom/ps. The logged fit also includes the production starting frame, which the trajectory does not store; in a 52-atom run this one end point moves the 50-ps slope by about 10^-3 meV/atom/ps. The check is reported as failed, as the rule states. **f**, Mean-squared displacement of Li, P, S and Cl in the four production runs at 1000 K (n = 4 runs, one per axes, titled with the model that drove it; averaged over all time origins and atoms of an element, centre-of-mass drift removed; no error bars). At the longest lag (199.95 ps, a single time origin) Li reaches at least 368 A^2, P at most 0.88 A^2 and Cl at most 1.32 A^2: the P framework and the Cl sublattice stay in place. S reaches 7.38 (MACE-MP-0), 2.14 (MatterSim), 0.90 (Gamma, stage 2) and 1.36 (2x2x2, stage 1) A^2; S moving further than P is consistent with reorientation of PS4 tetrahedra about fixed P. Sources: results/thermostat.csv, data/md/timeseries.csv.gz, data/md/msd.csv.gz.

## Extended Data Fig. 2. Re-analysis against the values published in July 2026

![Extended Data Fig. 2](../figures/extended/ed02_reproduction.png)

Extended Data Fig. 2 | Re-analysis against the values published in July 2026. The comparison follows a rule committed before any trajectory was re-analysed (protocol/reproduction_rule.md), applied to the 33 published runs of 11 series (x axis of a-d: series in the order of Fig. 1c, three runs each at 600, 800 and 1000 K). In a-d, f and g, marker shape is the run type (triangles, 52-atom cells; circles, the 416-atom, 200-ps production runs; inverted triangles, the 392-416-atom Cl-excess runs of 150 ps) and open markers (f, g) are the runs of the 2x2x2-label fine-tune (stage 1; every other model is filled); in a-c and f colour is the temperature. **a**, Relative difference between the re-analysed and the published pymatgen D of each run (n = 33; one value per run, no error bars). In 12 runs the two are bit-identical (drawn on the 'identical' row, at 1e-17); the others differ by 1.1e-16-7.3e-16, a few float64 rounding steps (dotted line, machine epsilon 2.22e-16). Solid line, the R1 limit (1e-9); dashed line, the R2 limit (1e-6). Classes: R1 for every run in D and in sigma. **b**, Relative difference of the kinisi D (seed 0 here, an unseeded sampler in July) and **c**, of its kinisi standard deviation (n = 33 runs each), with each run's threshold max(3 s_seed, 2 %) and max(3 s_seed, 10 %) (black bars), where s_seed is the relative standard deviation over seeds 1-10 (n = 10; grey bars, 3 s_seed when below the floor; dashed line, the floor). Within the threshold: 33 of 33 runs in b and 33 of 33 in c (class R2). The closest is MatterSim, 52 atoms, 50 ps at 800 K in b (2.331 % against 2.332 %, 0.9994 of the threshold) and MACE-MP-0, 52 atoms, 50 ps at 1000 K in c (0.533 of the threshold); in c, 3 s_seed never exceeds 7.36 %, so the 10 % floor sets every threshold. **d**, The n = 11 Arrhenius fits (one per series, three temperatures each) re-done with the re-analysed values: |d ln sigma(300 K)| in units of the published log half-width of the 1-sigma interval (black, left of each series) and |d Ea| in units of the published Ea error (grey, right). Light band, R2-; darker band, R3. Solid line, the R2 limit (0.1); dashed line, the R2- limit (1). Classes: R2; the largest difference is 0.050 (MatterSim, 416 atoms, 200 ps). The published values are therefore quoted for these series (rule item 2). **e**, Force RMSE written in the MACE training logs minus the same error re-evaluated from the model files (meV/A), on the validation set (n = 5 models) and on the training set (n = 4; MACE-MP-0 has no training log), for the four fine-tuned models (colour, model; stage 1 open, stage 2 filled) and the foundation model before fine-tuning (validation set of the Gamma fine-tune). Grey bands, half the last printed digit. Validation errors agree to within 0.040 meV/A. The logged training errors of the Gamma fine-tune (asterisks) cover 20 of its 22 training configurations because MACE drops the last incomplete batch (protocol amendment A1); against all 22 they differ by +0.22 and -0.03 meV/A, and 11 (stage 1) and 21 (stage 2) of the 231 subsets of 20 configurations reproduce the logged values exactly. **f**, Thermostat statistics recomputed from the trajectory against the n = 19 surviving July run logs (4 of them belong to runs never analysed in July; per run in Extended Data Fig. 1e): absolute difference in units of the tolerance of the rule (0.2 K for 392-416 atoms and 1 K for 52 atoms for the mean temperature; one unit of the logged rounding, 0.0001 eV/atom and 0.001 meV/atom/ps, for the mean energy and the drift; runs spread horizontally at random within each column). The mean temperature agrees in 19 of 19 runs and the mean energy in 19 of 19; the drift agrees in 15 of 19. The 4 drift values outside the tolerance (mace_52_050_800K, mace_52_050_1000K, mattersim_52_050_800K, mattersim_52_050_1000K; at most 0.0015 meV/atom/ps) are all from 52-atom, 50-ps runs, where the logged fit also includes the starting frame that the trajectory does not store; the check is reported as failed, as the rule states. **g**, Monte-Carlo scatter of kinisi D, s_seed (relative standard deviation of D over seeds 1-10, n = 10 per run; seed 0 is the primary value), against the relative width of the kinisi posterior (posterior standard deviation over D, seed 0), for all n = 42 runs (colour, the model that drove the run). The rule accepts a kinisi D within max(3 s_seed, 2 %); above the dashed line (s_seed = 0.667 %, where 3 s_seed = 2 %) the seed term sets the threshold, which is the case in 10 of 42 runs (9 of the 18 52-atom runs and Fine-tuned on Gamma labels, 416 atoms, 200 ps at 600 K). s_seed is 0.12-1.30 %, 0.020-0.055 times the posterior width. Sources: results/reproduction_runs.csv, results/reproduction_fits.csv, results/thermostat.csv, data/models/log_reproduction.csv, data/dft/configs.csv, data/md/transport.csv, data/md/kinisi_seeds.csv, protocol/reproduction_rule.md, protocol/amendments.md.

## Extended Data Fig. 3. Arrhenius fits of every series

![Extended Data Fig. 3](../figures/extended/ed03_arrhenius.png)

Extended Data Fig. 3 | Arrhenius fits of every series. One panel per MD series (n = 3 runs each, one per temperature), grouped by part of the protocol. **a**, **b**, **c**, MACE-MP-0 in 52-atom cells run for 50, 100 and 150 ps (independent trajectories) and **d**, its 416-atom, 200-ps production runs; **e**, **f**, **g**, **h**, the same for MatterSim (the universal potentials on Li6PS5Cl); **i**, MACE-MP-0 fine-tuned on the Gamma labels (stage two) and **j**, on the 2x2x2 labels (stage one), both under the production protocol; **k**, **l**, **m**, **n**, the Cl-excess series Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) under MACE-MP-0 with x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 (summarised in Extended Data Fig. 9). Markers, conductivity of each run at 600, 800 and 1000 K from the pymatgen diffusion coefficient (Nernst-Einstein, no Haven ratio); colour, model (Cl content for the Cl-excess series); shape, run type (circle, 416-atom production run; triangle, 52-atom run; inverted triangle, Cl-excess run); open, the stage-one model. Error bars, the kinisi 1-sigma uncertainty, whose ratio to sigma weights the fit of ln(sigma T) against 1/T. Line, the quoted fit (solid over the simulated range, dashed where extrapolated to 300 K) with its 1-sigma band from the fit covariance; the value printed in each panel is sigma(300 K) with its 1-sigma interval and Ea with its 1-sigma error. The temperatures of the outer data columns and of the extrapolation target are written above the data. The quoted fit is the published one for every series analysed in July 2026 and the re-analysis otherwise (MACE-MP-0, 52 atoms, 100 ps; MatterSim, 52 atoms, 100 ps; Fine-tuned on 2x2x2 labels, 416 atoms, 200 ps). Strips, residual ln sigma minus the quoted fit at each temperature in units of that point's ln-space uncertainty (kinisi standard deviation over sigma, from the re-analysis also for the published fits); grey band, +/-1. With three temperatures and two parameters each fit has one degree of freedom; the largest residual is -2.68 (MACE-MP-0, 52 atoms, 50 ps, 800 K). Shared logarithmic conductivity axis in all panels. Sources: results/fits.csv, data/md/transport.csv.

## Extended Data Fig. 4. Sampling and estimator checks

![Extended Data Fig. 4](../figures/extended/ed04_sampling.png)

Extended Data Fig. 4 | Sampling and estimator checks. Every run is a single trajectory per temperature; D is the Li tracer diffusion coefficient. **a**, Root-mean-square difference of the atomic positions between two runs with the same potential, cell and temperature, against production time (n = 21 pairs: 18 among the 52-atom runs of 50, 100 and 150 ps, three per universal potential and temperature, and the 416-atom, 200-ps MACE-MP-0 production run against the 416-atom Cl-excess x = 0 run at each temperature, thick lines). Positions are stored at frames 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 500 (one frame every 50 fs); the axis is linear below 0.05 ps and logarithmic above. At the first production frame the pairs already differ by 1.55-3.32 A (52 atoms) and 2.46-4.96 A (416 atoms), and by 2.46-10.00 A after 25 ps, so the runs are independent trajectories and not extensions of one another. **b**, pymatgen D of the four consecutive 50-ps blocks of each 416-atom, 200-ps production run divided by the value from the full run (n = 48 blocks of 4 runs at 3 temperatures; blocks in time order from left to right; logarithmic axis; pymatgen gives no uncertainty, so no error bars). The ratio is 1.02-3.09 at 600 K; 0.95-1.44 at 800 K; 0.78-1.12 at 1000 K. At 600 K the slower models give block values well above the full-run value, i.e. pymatgen D still depends on the length of the analysed window there. **c**, kinisi D of the same runs with the fit window starting at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 % of the run, divided by the primary value (start at 30 %, grey line; n = 5 starts for each of 12 runs); error bars, kinisi posterior standard deviation divided by the same primary value. Above 600 K the ratio stays within 0.91-1.13; the largest change is 1.78 (Fine-tuned on Gamma labels, 416 atoms, 200 ps, 600 K, start 0.1). **d**, pymatgen D against kinisi D for all 42 runs (dashed line, equality; no error bars: the kinisi posterior standard deviation is 5-35 % of D). Colour, potential; circles, the 416-atom production runs; triangles, the 52-atom runs; inverted triangles, the four 150-ps Cl-excess runs of MACE-MP-0 (x = 0-0.75, Extended Data Fig. 9). pymatgen D / kinisi D is 1.00-2.26 at 600 K; 1.07-1.89 at 800 K; 0.96-1.29 at 1000 K (largest 2.26, Fine-tuned on Gamma labels, 416 atoms, 200 ps, 600 K). **e**, sigma(300 K) extrapolated from weighted Arrhenius fits of the pymatgen conductivity at 600, 800 and 1000 K (weights from the kinisi relative standard deviation; the full-run fits are those of Extended Data Fig. 3) against simulated time per run (n = 15 fits, each on 3 runs); error bars, the 1-sigma interval propagated from the fit covariance. Triangles, the 52-atom runs (MACE-MP-0 22.5, 2.44, 12.5 and MatterSim 14.1, 2.51, 1.79 mS/cm at 50, 100 and 150 ps); circles joined by lines, the 416-atom production run truncated to its first 50, 100 and 150 ps and in full (MACE-MP-0 16.3, 13.5, 8.43, 5.54, MatterSim 3.90, 1.31, 0.485, 0.344 mS/cm); inverted triangle, the second 416-atom MACE-MP-0 run (Cl-excess x = 0, 150 ps, 7.30 mS/cm). The truncated windows are nested parts of one trajectory, and markers at the same simulated time are offset horizontally. **f**, Activation energy of the same fits; error bars, 1 standard deviation of the fitted slope (production windows: MACE-MP-0 0.223, 0.231, 0.249, 0.266 eV, MatterSim 0.258, 0.296, 0.333, 0.346 eV; 52-atom runs 0.213-0.302 eV). **g**, kinisi D (seed 0, fitted from 30 % of the run) of the 52-atom runs, which have the 52-atom cell of the AIMD reference (Extended Data Fig. 8) at a 6 % larger volume, and of the second 416-atom MACE-MP-0 run, divided by the AIMD kinisi D at the same temperature (n = 21 ratios); error bars, the ratio times the two relative standard deviations added in quadrature. Within each temperature, from left: MACE-MP-0 52-atom runs of 50, 100 and 150 ps and the second 416-atom run, then MatterSim 52-atom runs of 50, 100 and 150 ps. At 800 and 1000 K the 52-atom runs give 2.72-6.90 (MACE-MP-0) and 1.48-2.68 (MatterSim), the second run 3.32-5.02; the production runs are compared in Fig. 3. Grey column, at 600 K the AIMD Li MSD is almost flat in the fit window (log-log slope 0.0708): those ratios compare caged motion, not diffusion coefficients (Extended Data Fig. 8 shows all AIMD temperatures). **h**, Li mean-squared displacement against lag time at 600 and 1000 K (all time origins, centre-of-mass drift removed) of AIMD (black) and of the 100-ps, 52-atom runs that match the AIMD length and cell (one trajectory each; log-log slope in the fit window 0.641 and 0.997 for MACE-MP-0 and 0.404 and 0.866 for MatterSim at 600 and 1000 K; AIMD slope printed in each panel). ## Extended Data Fig. 5. The two DFT label sets

![Extended Data Fig. 5](../figures/extended/ed05_labels.png)

Extended Data Fig. 5 | The two DFT label sets. Both sets label the same 27 configurations with Quantum ESPRESSO 7.1 (GBRV ultrasoft PBE pseudopotentials, 60/480 Ry, Gaussian smearing 0.01 Ry, convergence threshold 1e-7 Ry) and differ only in the k-point sampling: Gamma point only, or a 2x2x2 Monkhorst-Pack mesh (taken as the reference). **a**, The 27 labelled configurations, frames 100-900 of the 52-atom, 50-ps MACE-MP-0 runs at 600, 800 and 1000 K, by subset: T22, trained on by both fine-tunes (n = 22); H3, held out by both (n = 3: T600_f400, T800_f200, T800_f500), the primary test set; H2, held out by the Gamma fine-tune only (n = 2). No 1000 K configuration is held out. **b**, Gamma minus 2x2x2 for each of the 27 configurations, ordered by source temperature and frame and coloured by subset as in **a** (H3 and H2 columns shaded): energy per atom (4.18 to 6.04 meV/atom; dashed line, the mean offset over T22, 5.09 meV/atom, which the energy comparisons subtract; centred RMSE over All27 0.43 meV/atom), force RMSE over all components of a configuration (dashed line, the All27 value 17.2 meV/A, the label floor used in Fig. 2; largest 24.3 meV/A for T1000_f900) and pressure (RMSE 0.47 kbar; the Gamma pressure is the higher one for every configuration). Single values per configuration, no error bars. **c**, Gamma against 2x2x2 force components of all atoms of the 27 configurations, by element (n = 648 Li, 108 P, 540 S, 108 Cl atoms, three components each); RMSE (meV/A) and least-squares slope through the origin: Li 8.4 (slope 0.999), P 20.3 (slope 1.005), S 23.7 (slope 1.002), Cl 13.9 (slope 0.996). Dashed line, identity. **d**, Cost of the SCF single points: wall time of each configuration (n = 27 per label set; horizontal line, median: 28 min with 1 k-point on 16 MPI processes; 5.2 h with 8 k-points on 32 processes; 200 and 4525 core-hours for the 27 configurations) and the number of SCF iterations (12-13 and 11-13). The 2x2x2 wall and CPU times are printed by Quantum ESPRESSO in hours and minutes, so they are resolved to 1 min. **e**, Distribution of the 2x2x2 force magnitudes per element over the 27 configurations (bins of 0.2 eV/A; atoms per element in the legend; mean Li 0.68, P 2.22, S 1.26, Cl 0.66 eV/A); the Gamma distributions are indistinguishable at this scale (mean magnitudes differ by at most 11.4 meV/A). Sources: data/dft/configs.csv, data/dft/qe_runs.csv, data/dft/pseudopotentials.csv, results/label_floor.csv, results/label_floor_configs.csv, data/models/predictions_forces.csv.gz.

## Extended Data Fig. 6. Training records of the two fine-tunes

![Extended Data Fig. 6](../figures/extended/ed06_training.png)

Extended Data Fig. 6 | Training records of the two fine-tunes. Both start from MACE-MP-0 small with the same settings (batch size 4; stage one with energy and force loss weights 1 and 10 and learning rate 0.0001; stage two, from epoch 90 (shaded), with weights 1000 and 100, learning rate 0.001 and stochastic weight averaging). **a**, Validation force RMSE and **b**, validation energy RMSE per atom against epoch, as written by MACE: one training run per fine-tune, each point a single evaluation of the whole validation set, so there are no error bars. The two curves use different validation sets and different labels and are not directly comparable: the Gamma fine-tune is validated on n = 5 configurations (V5 = H3 + H2) against the Gamma labels, the 2x2x2 fine-tune on n = 3 (H3) against the 2x2x2 labels. Red circles at 'start', MACE-MP-0 small before fine-tuning on the same validation sets (234.4 and 216.2 meV/A; dotted, joined to the first epoch). The energy error before training is not drawn because it is an absolute energy error of the foundation model (it depends on the reference energies), which this study does not report. Large circles, the selected models, coloured by model as in the table (c); open, stage one (epoch 89 for both; 78.9 and 70.3 meV/A); filled, stage two (epochs 116 and 119; 62.4 and 57.1 meV/A). The switch to the stage-two weights and learning rate raises the force error transiently (to 131 and 168 meV/A). Logarithmic energy axis in b. **c**, Errors in the training logs against the same errors re-evaluated from the model files in float64 on a CPU, as root-mean-square errors over the n configurations of each set (validation n = 5 for V5 and 3 for H3; training n = 22 and 24). Validation errors agree to within 0.04 meV/A (the logs print one decimal). The logged training errors of the Gamma fine-tune cover 20 of its 22 training configurations, because MACE drops the last incomplete batch of the shuffled training loader (asterisks; protocol amendment A1): 11 and 21 of the 231 subsets of 20 configurations reproduce the logged stage-one and stage-two values. The 2x2x2 fine-tune has 24 training configurations, a multiple of the batch size, and its logged training errors cover all of them. 'Gamma' and '2x2x2' denote MACE-MP-0 small fine-tuned on the Gamma-point labels (22 training and 5 validation configurations) or on the 2x2x2 labels (24 and 3); stage 1 is the best epoch before stochastic weight averaging, stage 2 the model after it. The two models that drove MD differ in stage (Gamma, stage 2; 2x2x2, stage 1); the effect of the stage on the force error is shown in Fig. 4. Sources: data/models/training/ftG_record.jsonl, data/models/training/ftK_record.jsonl, data/models/evaluation.json, data/models/log_reproduction.csv, data/dft/configs.csv.

## Extended Data Fig. 7. Model identity and the full cross-evaluation

![Extended Data Fig. 7](../figures/extended/ed07_models.png)

Extended Data Fig. 7 | Model identity and the full cross-evaluation. Markers: colour by model, filled for MACE-MP-0 and stage 2, open for stage 1 (legend at top). 'Gamma' and '2x2x2' denote MACE-MP-0 small fine-tuned on the Gamma-point labels (22 training and 5 validation configurations) or on the 2x2x2 labels (24 and 3); stage 1 is the best epoch before stochastic weight averaging, stage 2 the model after it. **a**, Force fingerprints of the 416-atom, 200-ps MD runs at 600, 800 and 1000 K (n = 9 runs): RMS difference between the forces stored in four frames of each run (first, one third, two thirds, last) and the forces of each candidate model recomputed in float32 on a CPU (logarithmic axis). A run is assigned to a model if the residual is below 1 meV/A (dashed line) and every other candidate is at least 10 times worse. The matching model gives 0.0006-0.0007 meV/A, the next best 15.7-227.7 meV/A. Assignments: MACE-MP-0 run -> MACE-MP-0; Gamma fine-tune run -> Gamma, stage 2; 2x2x2 fine-tune run -> 2x2x2, stage 1. These are the models of the MD runs in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 (MACE-MP-0; Gamma, stage 2; 2x2x2, stage 1); the other two fine-tuned models have no MD run. **b**, Force RMSE (meV/A, all force components of the n configurations under each column) of all five models against both label sets on each subset. Own validation is defined for the fine-tunes only: V5 = H3 + H2 for the Gamma fine-tune, H3 for the 2x2x2 fine-tune. Shading is logarithmic in the RMSE. Italic values include configurations the model was trained on; the primary estimand is the H3 column against 2x2x2 (MACE-MP-0 216.2; Gamma, stage 2 59.3; 2x2x2, stage 1 70.3; Gamma, stage 1 72.8; 2x2x2, stage 2 57.1), as in Fig. 2. **c**, Softening slope (least-squares slope through the origin of model against 2x2x2 force components) on H3, overall and per element (n = 468 components; Li 216, P 36, S 180, Cl 36). MACE-MP-0: all 0.81, Li 0.86, P 0.78, S 0.81, Cl 0.92; fine-tuned models 0.98-1.00. Line, slope 1. **d**, Pressure error against the 2x2x2 labels for each configuration (n = 27 per model; H3 large and opaque), a diagnostic only: no model was trained on stress. Numbers above, All27 RMSE (kbar): MACE-MP-0 1.02; Gamma, stage 2 4.46; 2x2x2, stage 1 4.07; Gamma, stage 1 4.66; 2x2x2, stage 2 4.74. The fine-tuned models underestimate the pressure by 4.0-4.7 kbar on average (MACE-MP-0: +0.64 kbar), well outside the label floor of 0.47 kbar (grey band). **e**, Decomposition of the force error against the two label sets, RMSE(m vs 2x2x2)^2 = RMSE(m vs Gamma)^2 + floor^2 + cross term, over all force components of H3 (large markers; floor 16.3 meV/A) and All27 (small markers; floor 17.2 meV/A). The cross term divided by floor^2 is 0 for a model whose error against the Gamma labels is uncorrelated with the Gamma minus 2x2x2 difference (it tracks the Gamma labels) and -2 for a model whose error against the 2x2x2 labels is uncorrelated with it (it tracks the 2x2x2 labels). H3 (All27): MACE-MP-0 -6.38 (-5.53); Gamma, stage 2 -1.44 (-0.97); 2x2x2, stage 1 -2.52 (-2.22); Gamma, stage 1 -1.55 (-1.28); 2x2x2, stage 2 -2.41 (-1.90). The Gamma fine-tunes lie between the two references, closer to 0 on All27, which contains their training configurations; the 2x2x2 fine-tunes lie near -2. MACE-MP-0, trained on neither label set, lies below -2: its error against the 2x2x2 labels is anticorrelated with the label difference. Single values, no error bars. Sources: data/models/fingerprints.csv, results/cross_evaluation.csv, results/cross_evaluation_configs.csv, results/label_floor.csv, results/floor_decomposition.csv, data/dft/configs.csv.

## Extended Data Fig. 8. The AIMD reference

![Extended Data Fig. 8](../figures/extended/ed08_aimd.png)

Extended Data Fig. 8 | The AIMD reference. Li transport of every model is compared with ab initio MD (AIMD) of the same ordered Li6PS5Cl cell (Li24P4S20Cl4, Cl on 4a, S on 4c; amendment A3): the trajectories of Deng et al. (Chem. Mater. 29, 281-288, 2017), published with the paper's notebooks (repository materialsvirtuallab/matgenb, commit 2e77d515f23c, BSD-3-Clause license, Copyright (c) 2017 Materials Virtual Lab) and re-analysed here with the estimators and settings of the MLIP runs. From the files: VASP, 52 atoms, time step 2 fs, every 10th step stored, 100 ps at each of 600, 800, 1000 and 1200 K; the exchange-correlation functional and the thermostat are not recorded. Differences from the MLIP runs: lattice parameter 10.10 A against 10.28 A (5.14 % smaller volume), 52 atoms against 416 for the production runs (the 52-atom MLIP runs match the AIMD cell; their ratios to AIMD are in Extended Data Fig. 4), one trajectory per temperature in both. The comparison of the four production models with this reference is Fig. 3. **a**, Mean-squared displacement of Li, P, S and Cl from the single trajectory at each temperature (n = 1; averaged over all time origins, centre-of-mass drift removed; no error bars); grey, the kinisi fit window (lags from 30 % of the run). The framework stays in place: at the longest lag P, S and Cl reach at most 0.612, 0.692 and 0.827 A^2 at any temperature. At 600 K the Li MSD is caged at 11.5-13.5 A^2 across the fit window. **b**, AIMD Li D against 1000/T, one trajectory per temperature: kinisi (seed 0; squares; error bars, the posterior standard deviation; 7.07e-07 +/- 3.10e-07, 4.30e-06 +/- 1.26e-06, 1.70e-05 +/- 3.01e-06, 4.19e-05 +/- 6.96e-06 cm^2/s) and pymatgen (dashes, drawn just right of the squares; no error estimate; 2.45e-06, 6.02e-06, 1.99e-05, 4.77e-05 cm^2/s), in the order 600, 800, 1000, 1200 K. Labels give the temperature and the log-log slope of the Li MSD in the fit window (0.0708 at 600 K, 0.523 at 800 K, 0.998 at 1000 K, 0.851 at 1200 K); a slope near 1 is diffusive. At 600 K (slope 0.0708, italic label 'caged') neither estimator measures a diffusion coefficient, so a 600 K ratio to AIMD is not a ratio of diffusion coefficients; the 1200 K run has no MLIP counterpart. **c**, kinisi D for seeds 1-10 (n = 10 per temperature; grey squares, jittered horizontally) relative to seed 0 (black bar); they span -1.86 to +2.96 %. s_seed, their relative standard deviation (1.21, 0.887, 0.538, 0.602 %), is 2.75-3.63 % of the posterior width (post., the relative posterior standard deviation of seed 0). **d**, Extrapolated sigma(300 K) of the ordered cell (logarithmic axis). Published AIMD extrapolations (black; squares, single values; bar, a published range) span 5.16 orders of magnitude (0.002 to 290 mS/cm; the first two as quoted in Table 2 of Baktash et al., npj Comput. Mater. 6, 162, 2020). This study's extrapolations for the two universal potentials (416-atom production runs, quoted fits over n = 3 temperatures; bars, the 1-sigma interval of the fit) give MACE-MP-0 5.55 [4.21, 7.31] and MatterSim 0.349 [0.249, 0.489] mS/cm. An extrapolated value is therefore not a usable reference, and models are compared through D at the simulated temperatures. Grey rows: measured room-temperature conductivities of S/Cl-disordered polycrystals (Wang et al. 2018, diamond; range compiled by Li et al. 2025, bar), shown only as context on the same axis; no ratio is formed with them, and the ordered cell is about two orders of magnitude less conductive than the disordered one in AIMD (Baktash et al. 2020). Literature values are printed as given in the sources. Sources: data/references/aimd_deng2017/transport.csv, data/references/aimd_deng2017/kinisi_seeds.csv, data/references/aimd_deng2017/msd.csv.gz, results/fits.csv, data/references/literature.csv, data/md/transport.csv.
